title: International Trade and the Balance of Payments

questions.question: According to David Ricardo's theory, a country gains from trade by specialising in goods where:
options: Its absolute output is the highest
questions.rationale: Comparative advantage says specialise where opportunity cost is lowest — gains from trade exist even for a country that is worse at producing everything.

questions.question: In the lesson's example, India's opportunity cost of 1 kg tea is:
questions.rationale: Tea costs India 10 hours and software 30, so each kg of tea forgoes 10/30 = 1/3 unit of software — lower than the USA's 1/2, so India exports tea.

questions.question: The balance of trade (BoT) refers to:
options: Exports minus imports of goods only
Exports minus imports of goods and services
questions.rationale: BoT is the merchandise balance — goods exports minus goods imports; services, income, and transfers are the invisibles that complete the current account.

questions.question: Software exports, tourism earnings, and workers' remittances are collectively called:
questions.rationale: Invisibles — services, income, and transfers — offset a good part of India's merchandise trade deficit.

questions.question: Since 1991, India's exchange rate regime is best described as:
options: A fixed peg to the US dollar
A managed float with RBI smoothing
questions.rationale: India operates a market-driven rate with the Reserve Bank intervening to smooth excessive volatility — a managed float.

questions.question: Depreciation of the rupee will most likely:
options: Make Indian exports cheaper abroad and imports costlier
Make exports costlier and imports cheaper
questions.rationale: A weaker rupee lowers the foreign-currency price of Indian exports and raises the rupee cost of imports such as crude oil — exporting import-inflation risk.

questions.question: Depreciation differs from devaluation in that depreciation is:
options: A policy decision by the government
A market-driven fall in the currency's value
questions.rationale: Depreciation happens through market demand and supply; devaluation is a deliberate policy cut of a pegged rate.

questions.question: The WTO became operational on 1 January 1995, replacing:
questions.rationale: The permanent World Trade Organization succeeded the provisional General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade of 1947, both headquartered in Geneva.

questions.question: Which of the following is an agreement covered by the WTO but not by GATT?
questions.rationale: GATT covered goods only; the WTO umbrella added services (GATS) and intellectual property (TRIPS) with binding dispute settlement.

questions.question: A physical limit on the quantity of a good that may be imported during a year is a:
questions.rationale: A quota caps import quantity directly — unlike a tariff, which raises the price instead.
